changes_made.explanation: Removed MENT as it's an evaluation dataset created from annotations, not a source dataset. Added CNN/DM which is used for training CMLM models. Kept only the summarization models being evaluated (BART, PEGASUS) and removed CMLM/ENTFA/CLM/MLM which are components of the evaluation methodology.
All metrics are correctly extracted and normalized. ROUGE evaluates summary quality, FEQA and DAE evaluate faithfulness, and ENFS (Entity Not Found in Source) measures hallucination.
No LLMs are used as judges. The paper uses pre-trained language models (MLM, CMLM) as components of their ENTFA system, but not as post-generation evaluators.

guideline: Manual entity-level annotation of 2,838 entities from BART-generated summaries
Three-way classification: non-hallucinated, factual hallucination, non-factual hallucination
Check inferability from source document using entailment
Verify factuality of hallucinated entities using external resources (Wikipedia, Google Search)
Calculate inter-annotator agreement using Fleiss' Kappa

changes_made.explanation: Expanded guideline to include specific annotation methodology and agreement metrics. Simplified criteria to core evaluation dimensions mentioned in annotation process.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on abstractive summarization evaluation with emphasis on entity-level factuality and hallucination detection. Human evaluation includes detailed entity-level annotation with specific criteria. Automatic evaluation uses standard summarization metrics plus faithfulness-specific tools. The ENTFA system uses MLM/CMLM probabilities but these are methodology components, not LLM-as-judge evaluation.
